definition: Profane means irreverent toward the sacred or solemn; laced with cursing.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word profane. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know profane should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The dictation app transcribed the plumber's profane muttering faithfully, and the emailed invoice arrived unprintable.
Irreverent is milder than profane — it smirks at solemn things but keeps its language clean.
Blasphemous is graver than profane: profane speech disrespects the sacred at large, while blasphemy insults the divine directly and by name.

Indecent means offending standards of decency — too explicit or improper for the setting, with no humor required. Profane cuts along different lines: coarse, swearing language, or irreverence toward what is sacred. A crude photograph is indecent; cursing in a sanctuary is profane, and neither has to involve the other.

Crude means rough and unrefined — language or manners that skip politeness without necessarily breaking any deeper rule. Profane goes further on two fronts: its coarseness rises to actual cursing, and it can violate the sacred itself. A crude joke is merely impolite; profane speech swears or desecrates.
